questions.question: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Camillo Golgi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Camillo Golgi** developed the black reaction technique (also known as Golgi's method) in 1873, which was a major advancement in neuroanatomy.
 
• This staining technique made it possible to visualize the detailed structure and organization of nerve cells and their intricate networks.
 
• The black reaction involves using silver chromate to stain a few cells in their entirety, allowing for the observation of individual neurons against a transparent background.
 
• This method was instrumental in establishing the neuron doctrine, which states that the neuron is the basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system.
 
• Golgi shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906 with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the structure of the nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Golgi apparatus**, an important cellular organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles, was also discovered by Camillo Golgi.
 
• Golgi's contributions to cell biology and neuroscience are foundational, with the Golgi method continuing to influence neuroscientific research well into the 20th century and beyond.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for understanding the complex connectivity and functions of the nervous system, influencing both basic science and clinical approaches to neurological diseases.
 
• The Golgi method's ability to selectively stain neurons is still appreciated for its utility in highlighting the intricate details of cell morphology and connectivity.

questions.question: The brick temple of Bhitargaon is situated in which state?

• The temple is notable for its **terraced basement** and the **earthenware** decorations that adorn its exterior.
 
• It is one of the **oldest surviving temples** in the country made entirely of brick.

• The temple's design and construction techniques have provided valuable insights into the **evolution of Hindu temple architecture** in India.
 
• Despite suffering damage over the centuries, including a partial collapse in the 19th century, the temple has been **partially restored** and continues to attract historians, archaeologists, and tourists.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to measure the total output of goods and services in an economy including depreciation during a specific period within country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is the total market value of all **final goods and services** produced within a country in a specific period.
 
• GDP includes **depreciation**, which is the decrease in value of an asset over time.
 
• **Depreciation** is factored into GDP to account for the wear and tear on capital goods over the period.
 
• By including depreciation, GDP provides a comprehensive overview of the **economic activity** within a country, making it a crucial indicator for economists and policymakers.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Net Domestic Product (NDP)
 Calculated as GDP minus depreciation. It represents the net value of all goods and services after accounting for the loss in value of capital goods.
 
 

 2) Gross National Product (GNP)
 Measures the total value of goods and services produced by residents of a country, regardless of the production location. It includes incomes earned abroad.
 
 

 3) Net National Product (NNP)
 GNP minus depreciation. It represents the net output of a nation's economy, accounting for the wear and tear on capital goods.

questions.question: The East-West corridor, which is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, links which two cities of India from the following?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **East-West Corridor** is a part of the larger Golden Quadrilateral project aimed at connecting the eastern and western parts of India through a high-speed road network.
 
• This corridor specifically links **Silchar** in Assam in the East to **Porbandar** in Gujarat in the West.
 
• The project is one of the most ambitious infrastructure projects in India, intended to facilitate faster transportation and contribute to the economic development of the regions it connects.
 
• The total length of the East-West Corridor is approximately **3,300 kilometers**, making it one of the longest road projects in India.
 
• It is implemented by the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)** under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral** is a highway network connecting most of the major industrial, agricultural, and cultural centers of India.
 
• It forms a quadrilateral linking the four major metropolitan cities of India: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.
 
• Overall, the Golden Quadrilateral covers a distance of about **5,846 kilometers**, making it one of the largest highway projects in the world.
 
• The project aims to reduce travel times, improve cargo movement, and connect rural and urban areas for economic growth.

questions.question: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?

options.text: Debit cards are used for online transactions, while credit cards are used for in-person purchases.
Credit cards require a PIN, while debit cards require a signature.
Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
Debit cards have higher interest rates than credit cards.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Debit cards** allow you to spend money by drawing on funds you have already deposited at the bank.
 
• **Debit cards** usually require a PIN (Personal Identification Number) for transactions, especially at ATMs and point-of-sale terminals.
 
• **Credit cards** may require a signature for transactions, but increasingly use PINs and contactless technology.
 
• Credit cards allow you to borrow money up to a certain limit, to be repaid later along with possible interest.
 
• **Interest rates** are applicable only to credit cards if the balance is not paid in full by the due date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debit card** transactions are directly deducted from the user's bank account.
 
• **Credit card** users can earn rewards, cash back, or air miles which may not be available with all debit cards.
 
• **Credit scores** can be positively or negatively affected by the use of credit cards, depending on the user's spending and repayment behavior.
 
• **Fraud protection** is strong for both credit and debit cards, but credit cards may offer more comprehensive protection in case of unauthorized transactions.
 
• **Overdraft fees** are generally not applicable to credit cards, but debit card users may face them if they opt into overdraft protection services and exceed their account balance.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 has included Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, includes the **Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran** communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of Tamil Nadu.
 
• This amendment aims to provide these communities with various **government benefits** and **programs** designed for Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Recognition as Scheduled Tribes helps in improving their social and economic status through **educational scholarships**, **employment reservations**, and other welfare measures.
 
• The inclusion reflects the government's commitment to recognizing the unique cultural and social identity of **indigenous communities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**
 Communities in India that are recognized by the constitution as socially and economically backward, and are given certain privileges and benefits.
 
 

 **Constitutional Amendment**
 A change or addition to the constitution. Amendments affecting the recognition of communities as Scheduled Tribes require legislation.
 
 

 **Welfare Measures**
 Programs and policies designed to support the well-being of disadvantaged sections of society, including educational, health, and economic benefits.
 
 

 **Social and Economic Status**
 The position of individuals or communities within the societal and economic hierarchy, often influencing their access to resources and opportunities.
 
 

 **Indigenous Communities**
 Groups of people who have historical ties to a particular region or country, often with distinct cultural, social, and economic practices.

options.text: Pandit Ravi Shankar and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar** was a world-renowned sitar player and composer, known for his pioneering work in bringing Indian classical music to the global stage.
 
• **Pandit Bhimsen Joshi** was a legendary vocalist in the Hindustani classical music tradition, known for his powerful voice and emotive performances.
 
• Both were awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, for their exceptional contributions to the field of music. Pandit Ravi Shankar received it in 1999, and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi in 2008.
 
• The **Bharat Ratna** is awarded for the highest degrees of national service, including artistic, literary, and scientific achievements, as well as recognition of public service of the highest order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Award
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Bharat Ratna**
 India's highest civilian award, established in 1954. It recognizes exceptional service towards the advancement of Art, Literature and Science, and in recognition of Public Service of the highest order.
 
 

 **Padma Awards**
 These are the second highest civilian awards in India after the Bharat Ratna, divided into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
 

 **National Awards**
 Includes a variety of awards presented by the Indian government to individuals and organizations for their contributions in various fields such as cinema, sports, education, science, and public services.
 
 

 **Gallantry Awards**
 Awards given for displaying conspicuous bravery or valor. They include the Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, and Vir Chakra.
 
 

 **Literary Awards**
 Includes awards like the Jnanpith Award and Sahitya Akademi Award, given for exceptional contributions to literature in various Indian languages.

questions.question: Which river is also known as Tsangpo?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Brahmaputra river** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **Brahmaputra river**.
 
• **Tsangpo** is the name given to the Brahmaputra river in Tibet, where it originates.
 
• It flows across southern Tibet to break through the Himalayas in great gorges and into Arunachal Pradesh (India) where it is known as **Dihang**.
 
• Upon entering Assam, the river is called **Brahmaputra** and is one of the major rivers in India.
 
• The Brahmaputra plays a crucial role in the ecosystem and economy of the region, supporting agriculture, transportation, and biodiversity.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Ganga river
 Originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand, India, and is considered one of the holiest rivers in Hinduism.
 
 

 2) Gandak river
 Originates near the Nepal-Tibet border and joins the Ganga in Bihar, India, contributing significantly to the Ganga basin.
 
 

 3) Kaveri river
 Originates in the Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, and flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, known for its cultural significance and as a lifeline for the agrarian economy in the region.

questions.question: What is the destination of the water drained off by the Nile river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Mediterranean Sea**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Nile River** is the longest river in the world, flowing through northeastern Africa.
 
• It has **two major tributaries**: the White Nile and the Blue Nile, which meet in Sudan.
 
• The river flows **northward through the desert**, creating a fertile valley across Egypt before draining into the Mediterranean Sea.
 
• The Nile's drainage into the Mediterranean Sea is crucial for **agriculture and civilization** in Egypt, providing fertile soil and supporting ancient and modern societies.

 [IMAGE: https://www.worldatlas.com/r/w768/upload/5e/1f/d6/nile-river-in-egypt-map.png] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Lake Victoria
 It is the source of the White Nile and is located in east-central Africa.
 
 

 Indian Ocean
 The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean, bounded by Asia, Africa, Australia, and the Southern Ocean, key for major global trade routes and rich in biodiversity. It significantly influences climate patterns, including the monsoon system, and faces environmental issues like overfishing and pollution.
 
 

 Lake Tanganyika
 One of the African Great Lakes, not directly connected to the Nile River system.

questions.question: Article 149 of the Constitution deals with _______.

options.text: the qualifications required for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 149** of the Indian Constitution specifically outlines the **duties and powers** of the Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) of India.
 
• The **CAG** is responsible for auditing all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund, and the Public Account, as well as all trading, manufacturing, profit and loss accounts, and balance sheets kept by any department of the Central or State governments.
 
• The CAG's role extends to auditing the receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and the State governments to ensure that the rules and guidelines are being followed.
 
• The CAG is also responsible for auditing any authority or body substantially financed by the government; this includes grants or loans given by the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Comptroller and Auditor-General** of India is an authority established by Article 148 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The CAG's main function is to audit the accounts of the Union and State governments and public sector organizations, and to ensure that public funds are being used efficiently.
 
• The appointment of the CAG is made by the President of India for a term of 6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CAG is considered the guardian of the public purse and plays a critical role in promoting accountability and transparency in government financial operations.
